outcome: urine volume at the first postoperative hour
Apgar score at the first minute
time to first requirement for analgesia
cohort: 100 patients undergoing elective cesarean section at a tertiary-level public hospital
finding: Spinal anesthesia was superior to general anesthesia in terms of postoperative comfort, as evidenced by faster recovery of bowel function, less blood loss, and longer time to first analgesia requirement.
mod_finding: This study found that in elective cesarean sections, spinal anesthesia was associated with a higher first-minute Apgar score compared to general anesthesia.
